A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey of Bayesian, neural and LLM-based temporal point processes. All pages, equations, tables, figures and references support comparison. Neither version contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reviews existing research without reporting original empirical results. Table 1 compares architectural properties and theoretical computational complexities.

after.justification: v2 remains a survey. Its performance statements and benchmark findings are attributed to cited studies, and its figures are explanatory illustrations. No original experiments or data analyses are reported.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an original algorithm or model. v2 expands descriptions of cited methods and supplies more explicit formulas for retained architectures; this does not establish a change to a proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Neither survey actually trains or evaluates models on datasets. TESRBench and DanmakuTPPBench are newly reviewed in v2 Section V-C, but their experiments belong to the cited studies.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. The conceptual recurrent-versus-autoregressive comparison in v1 Table 1 and v2 Table I retains the same model categories and entries.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocol is conducted in either version. v2's discussion of standardized evaluation in Section VIII cites another study and identifies a field-level limitation; it introduces no evaluation settings for this survey.

E4.justification: Neither version presents its own ablations, robustness tests or supplementary empirical analyses. v2's added discussions of missing events, observational noise and estimator failures summarize cited research.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Expanded discussion of Bayesian uncertainty and estimation theory introduces no empirical uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds qualitative findings attributed to cited studies, including improved event-description generation with temporal information in Language-TPP and multimodal performance gaps on DanmakuTPPBench (Sections V-B/C). These are additional literature-reported outcomes, without numerical score updates or same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 adds the explicit zero-triggering-kernel criterion for Granger noncausality and reviews approximation, generalization and posterior-consistency guarantees (Sections III-B, IV-A and VII-B). Core likelihood and branching derivations remain unchanged. Section IV-B also adds an O(1) KV-cached prediction claim without a supporting derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the same three-perspective survey contribution. The introduction extends claimed recent-work coverage from 2020–2024 to 2020–2025; the new conclusion largely consolidates the existing goals.

C2.justification: v2 substantially deepens critical interpretation through discussions of ODE/SDE solver costs, restrictions and failures of earlier score-matching estimators, causal-estimation pitfalls involving sparsity and observation resolution, and missing standardized benchmarks. These issues receive brief treatment or none in v1.

D1.justification: Where v1 describes embeddings and intensity decoders generally, v2 Sections IV-A/B specify sinusoidal time encodings, one-hot mark mappings, embedding combination and decoder parameters. These add implementation detail for reviewed models without establishing changed experiments. Neither version supplies a reproducibility package.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the reviewed literature: additional Bayesian and frequentist Hawkes inference approaches, neural theoretical results, 2025 LLM and multimodal work, and extensive causal-discovery methods. It also adds positioning relative to finance surveys.

P1.justification: v2 extensively expands and rewrites explanatory passages, promotes v1's LLM and training subsections into standalone Sections V and VI, subdivides applications, and adds a conclusion. The title changes 'Deep' to 'Neural', alongside author and document-style edits.

P2.justification: v1 has one table and no figures; v2 adds seven figures covering taxonomy, TPP functions, neural architectures, parameterizations, LLM integration, DanmakuTPPBench and applications. The existing table is retained and reformatted, and the document adopts a journal-style layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the survey's explanatory and critical value. Its structured causal-discovery coverage, explicit estimator failure conditions and model illustrations address important gaps in v1's brief treatments, making the review more useful for understanding applicability and tradeoffs. The new unsupported O(1) KV-caching claim in Section IV-B is a technical weakness, but its impact is limited relative to these gains.
